verification_method.principle: as_built_count was NOT taken from the manifests. Every count below was produced by scanning the source: 198 COBOL members, 18 copybooks, 131 JCL members, 27 PROCs, 18 sort control cards, 5 HLASM members, 4 PL/I members and 6 REXX execs.
verification_method.constructs_1_3_26_27: These four cannot be counted by pattern alone, so each declared placement was individually verified: for a fall-through, that the paragraph exists and that no matching -EXIT paragraph exists and which paragraph physically follows; for a hidden handler, its physical position in the paragraph list and the number of GO TO versus PERFORM references; for dead code, the PERFORM and GO TO counts and whether the gating switch is ever MOVEd to; for a dormant feature, the declared VALUE and whether the switch is ever MOVEd to. The verification result is carried on each placement.
verification_method.all_others: Counted by pattern over the stripped source (comment lines removed) — REDEFINES, 66 RENAMES, 88 VALUE ... THRU, OCCURS DEPENDING ON, COPY inside a copybook, CALL by identifier, OPEN EXTEND, INSPECT, STRING/UNSTRING, ROUNDED, PC-CC, YYDDD, SORT ... INPUT PROCEDURE — and over the JCL for symbolics, relative GDG references, STEPLIB depth and step-qualified DD overrides.
verification_method.counting_unit: Stated per construct in as_built_unit. The units are not the same across constructs and were never intended to be: a REDEFINES is counted as a clause, a fall-through as a placement.

gap_1_missing_called_subprograms.title: Missing called subprograms
gap_1_missing_called_subprograms.finding: An estate scan of CALL 'literal' targets against the basename of every source member found 12 statically-called subprogram names with no source anywhere in the tree, across 519 call sites. The batch estate could not link or run without them.
gap_1_missing_called_subprograms.resolution: Each was reconstructed as a working OS/VS COBOL 1974 subprogram in BATCH/COMMON/. Parameter lists were derived from the call sites - the operand lists, the operand PIC clauses, the return-code tests the callers make, and the fields the callers read back after the CALL. Signatures are fixed by the call sites and must not be changed.
gap_1_missing_called_subprograms.standards_exception: CABS-STD-041. These are subprograms entered by CALL inside another program's run unit. They have no job step, no CTLOUT allocation and no balance to strike, so the mandatory P0000-MAINLINE / P8000-CONTROL / CTLOUT structure in CONVENTIONS.md does not apply. Every header block states the exception and every prose block confirms the calling program's balancing equation is unaffected. CABCTLWR writes to a separate DD, CTLAUX, that no balancing process reads.

gap_2_dfsort_control_cards.title: Sort control cards use DFSORT syntax the target sort cannot parse
gap_2_dfsort_control_cards.finding: Of the 18 members in JCL/CTLCARDS/, only CABSRT04 is executable on MVT-era OS/360 Sort/Merge. The other 17 use INCLUDE, OMIT, SUM, INREC, OUTREC, OUTFIL, FIELDS=COPY, OPTION EQUALS or OPTION VLSHRT, none of which that sort supports. Separately, CABSRT11, CABSRT12 and CABSRT15 named four exit modules - CABSXJUR, CABSXZIP, CABSXBST, CABSXLST - that had no source anywhere in the tree.
gap_2_dfsort_control_cards.resolution: Agreed design, applied without deviation. (1) The DFSORT-syntax cards were KEPT WHERE THEY ARE, UNCHANGED - they are realistic, and they are the historical record of what each business rule is. Nothing was renamed. (2) A parallel runnable set was added in JCL/CTLCARDS/MVT/ using only SORT FIELDS= / MERGE FIELDS=, RECORD TYPE=/LENGTH=, MODS= and END. (3) Every rule the DFSORT card expressed declaratively was moved into an E15 or E35 exit in SORTEXIT/. (4) The four named-but-missing exits were written. (5) Fifteen further exits were written to carry the moved rules.

gap_2_dfsort_control_cards.modernization_implication: A transformation reading only the control cards will miss this logic: after the move the MVT cards are four lines of sort keys, record lengths and module names, with no INCLUDE to parse, no SUM to map to a GROUP BY and no OUTREC to map to a projection. A transformation reading only the COBOL will also miss it: none of these rules is coded in any COBOL program in the estate, and each program is individually a correct and complete reading of itself. The rules now live in a third place that neither path traverses - 19 load modules referenced only by the MODS operand of a control card, invoked only by the sort program, and never named in a CALL statement anywhere. The only path that reaches them is JCL step -> SYSIN DD -> control card member -> MODS operand -> load module name -> source member, four indirections, three of which are text in a data file rather than a language construct. Eleven distinct business rules are affected. Enumerate the exits from the MODS operands before any code analysis begins; the control cards are the only index that exists.
